answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in the vault and pays a saffron-stamped tax for a step on the spiral stair. The stair winds up: the k-th pays 40+8(k-1); first 40, thousandth 8,032. Auditors replay the stair; a reused saffron stamp, skipped step, or one key on two steps burns the bond. Forging 1,000 identities costs 4,036,000 plus 70,000 locked, against a 40,000 pool, so bulk fakery loses money. Honest agents pay 40 once and reclaim the bond.
